questions.question: Which pair shows the SAME amount?
questions.explain: 2 dimes is 20 cents and 4 nickels is also 20 cents, so they match. The trap is counting coins instead of adding their values.

questions.question: Which two groups are the same amount?
questions.explain: 1 dime is 10 cents and 2 nickels is 10 cents, so they are the same. Adding coin values, not counting coins, is the key.

questions.question: Do 2 quarters and 4 dimes show the same amount?
questions.explain: 2 quarters is 50 cents but 4 dimes is only 40 cents, so they are not the same. Do not just count the coins; add up the values.

questions.question: Which group has the SAME total as 1 quarter?
questions.explain: 2 dimes (20) plus 1 nickel (5) makes 25, the same as 1 quarter. Watch out for picking the group with the most coins.

questions.question: Mia has 2 dimes. Tom has 4 nickels. Who has more money?
questions.explain: 2 dimes is 20 cents and 4 nickels is also 20 cents, so they have the same. More coins does not always mean more money.

questions.question: Sam has 4 dimes. Ana has 1 quarter and 1 nickel. Do they have the same amount?
options: No, Sam has 40 and Ana has 30
No, Sam has 4 coins and Ana has 2 coins
questions.explain: 4 dimes is 40 cents but 1 quarter and 1 nickel is 30 cents, so they are different. Count the values, not the number of coins.

questions.question: Dad gives 2 quarters for a toy. Mom gives 4 dimes and 2 nickels. Did they give the same amount?
options: No, Dad gives 2 coins and Mom gives 6 coins
No, Dad gives 20 and Mom gives 60
No, Mom gives more because she has 4 dimes
questions.explain: 2 quarters is 50 and 4 dimes plus 2 nickels is 40 plus 10, which is also 50. Both give the same even though the coin counts differ.

questions.question: Zoe says, I have 3 dimes. My brother has 6 nickels. I have fewer coins, so I have less money. What is wrong with Zoe's thinking?
options: 3 dimes is 3 and 6 nickels is 6, so brother wins
6 nickels is 60, so brother has more money
3 dimes is 30 and 6 nickels is 6, so Zoe wins
3 dimes is 30, and 6 nickels is 30 too
questions.explain: 3 dimes is 30 and 6 nickels is also 30, so they are the same amount. Counting coins instead of adding values leads to the wrong answer.

questions.question: Mia has 2 quarters. She trades them for dimes. Her friend says she should get 4 dimes. Is the friend right?
options: No, 50 is not the same as 40
Yes, 4 is more than 2, so more
questions.explain: 2 quarters is 50 cents but 4 dimes is only 40 cents, so the friend is wrong. More dimes does not mean more value if the total is less.

questions.question: A card costs 30 cents. Sam pays 3 dimes. Tom pays 1 quarter and 1 nickel. Priya pays 2 dimes and 1 nickel. Who pays the wrong amount?
questions.explain: 3 dimes is 30 and 1 quarter plus 1 nickel is 30, but 2 dimes plus 1 nickel is only 25, so Priya is short. Add each coin's value to check.

questions.question: Leo has 50 cents. He says, I have 5 dimes. His sister says, I can make 50 with 2 quarters. Are they both right?
questions.explain: 5 dimes is 50 and 2 quarters is also 50, so both are correct. Do not just count the coins; add up what each one is worth.

questions.question: Ava pays 45 cents for a pencil with 1 quarter and 2 dimes. Leo wants to pay the same amount with other coins. Which group should Leo use?
questions.explain: Ava's coins are 25, 35, 45 cents. Count dimes and a nickel the same way: 10, 20, 30, 40, 45 — that is 4 dimes and 1 nickel. Matching the number of coins does not match the amount.

questions.question: Noah has 4 dimes and 2 nickels in his piggy bank. He wants to show the same amount with quarters and nickels. Which group is the same amount?
questions.explain: Noah has 10, 20, 30, 40, 45, 50 cents. One quarter and 5 nickels is 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50 — the same 50 cents. Add what the coins are worth, not how many coins you see.

questions.question: Priya saved 60 cents in 2 quarters and 1 dime. She wants to show the same amount with only dimes and nickels. Which group should she pick?
questions.explain: Priya has 25, 50, 60 cents. Five dimes and 2 nickels is 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 55, 60 — the same amount. A pile with more coins can still be worth less.

questions.question: Nora has 8 dimes for the bus, but the machine takes only quarters and nickels. The ride costs 80 cents. Which group should she use?
questions.explain: Three quarters is 25, 50, 75, and one more nickel makes 80 cents. Nine nickels looks like a lot of coins but is only 45 cents, so more coins is not more money.
